queries: WITH g AS (SELECT o.timespan, AVG(f.rebrate / NULLIF(f.feerate, 0)) AS avg_ratio, COUNT(*) AS match_count FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.timespan), a AS (SELECT timespan, avg_ratio, match_count, AVG(match_count) OVER () AS avg_match_count FROM g) SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS avg_of_avg_ratios, SUM(match_count) AS total_match_count, AVG(match_count - avg_match_count) AS avg_excess_over_mean FROM a WHERE match_count > avg_match_count

WITH g AS (SELECT o.timespan, AVG(f.rebrate / NULLIF(f.feerate, 0)) AS avg_ratio, COUNT(*) AS match_cnt FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.timespan), t AS (SELECT timespan, avg_ratio, match_cnt, AVG(match_cnt) OVER () AS avg_cnt FROM g) SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS avg_of_avg_ratios, SUM(match_cnt) AS total_match_count, AVG(match_cnt - avg_cnt) AS avg_excess_over_mean FROM t WHERE match_cnt > avg_cnt

WITH g AS (SELECT o.timespan, AVG(f.rebrate / NULLIF(f.feerate, 0)) AS avg_ratio, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.timespan), a AS (SELECT AVG(cnt * 1.0) AS avg_cnt FROM g) SELECT AVG(g.avg_ratio) AS avg_of_avg_ratios, SUM(g.cnt) AS total_match_count, AVG(g.cnt - a.avg_cnt) AS avg_excess_over_mean FROM g CROSS JOIN a WHERE g.cnt > a.avg_cnt

assumptions.assumption: A match is one fee row joined to its order, so the match count is COUNT(*) per timespan group. Orders with no fees add nothing.
A feerate of 0 is treated as a missing ratio (NULLIF) so the division doesn't fail. Those rows are ignored in the average but still counted as matches.
The cross-group average match count is the mean of the per-group counts, not a per-row average. A NULL timespan, if present, counts as its own group.

assumptions.assumption: Match count is the number of joined fee-order rows in each timespan group. The cross-group average is the mean of those group counts, not a per-row average.
A feerate of 0 makes the ratio undefined, so it is treated as missing (NULLIF) and left out of the average. This avoids a division-by-zero error.
Orders with a NULL timespan, if any, form their own group and count as a group in the cross-group average.

responses.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT o.timespan, AVG(f.rebrate / NULLIF(f.feerate, 0)) AS avg_ratio, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.timespan), a AS (SELECT AVG(cnt * 1.0) AS avg_cnt FROM g) SELECT AVG(g.avg_ratio) AS avg_of_avg_ratios, SUM(g.cnt) AS total_match_count, AVG(g.cnt - a.avg_cnt) AS avg_excess_over_mean FROM g CROSS JOIN a WHERE g.cnt > a.avg_cnt

assumptions.assumption: The cross-group average match count is the mean of the per-group counts (each group weighted equally), not the average per order or per fee row.
A match count is the number of joined fee-order rows in the group. Each fee row counts once, including rows whose ratio is missing.
A ratio is missing if rebrate or feerate is NULL. A feerate of 0 is also treated as missing (via NULLIF) to avoid division by zero.
Orders with a NULL timespan form their own group, as GROUP BY does by default.
